title: sverify report
description: A report as Report.to_json writes it and Report.from_json reads it (#736). Format 4. Within 1.x the format only gains optional keys, values from a fixed set may gain new values, and readers ignore keys they do not know (docs/stability.md). Conditions appear as their labels, the text str(report) prints. Postconditions, issues and assumptions are findings in the shape of a SARIF 2.1.0 result (#793): ruleId, level, kind, message.text, and sverify's own fields under properties.

format.description: The version of this format. Format 3 gave verdict the Verdict's value and added summary; format 4 named equivalence lenses and made facts and a postcondition's needs objects; formats 2 and 3 are still read.

sverify.description: The version of sverify that wrote the report.

proved.description: Derived from verdict: false for unproved, true for proved and proved_with_checks. Kept for readers of format 2; dropped at 2.0.

verdict.description: Report.verdict: "proved" (no run raises), "proved_with_checks" (a run stops where a check of the assumed issues fails on the data) or "unproved". In format 2 this held the first line of the report, which summary holds from format 3, so a reader accepts any string.

summary.description: The report's first line, for display: "proved", or "NOT proved: " and what is missing, counted. Tools read verdict and the findings.

engine_version.description: The engine version the profile of semantics describes, the version its facts were probed at (Report.engine_version); null under the reference and substrait.

semantics.description: The semantics the report is under. 1.x may add values.

dialect.description: The language of the transformation, which the labels and code are written in.

on_inferred.description: What the inferred preconditions do to the proof (verify(on_inferred=...)).

lenses.description: What the result's consumer observes (Report.lenses); a report written before the name lenses calls it equivalence.

deterministic.description: Whether every result the reference allows is one up to row order and up to the member of each class of doubles, -0.0 and 0.0 and every NaN (Report.deterministic, D48): no ties in an ORDER BY a window, an ordered aggregate or a LIMIT reads, no expression that tells the members of a picked class apart, and no other value the reference leaves open.

deterministic_exact.description: Whether every result the reference allows is one up to row order, the member of each class of doubles included: deterministic with no class pick (ties.places is empty).

class_places.description: What the class level leaves open (Report.deterministic): ties, and expressions that read a picked double.

kind.description: tie: the order of ties is open; class: a pick among the members of a class of doubles (D48); open: what the class level leaves open.

rows.description: At most this many output rows; null if nothing bounds them.

params.description: The ibis.param values the transformation was verified with, as `name (type) = value`.

requires.description: The preconditions assumed, as labels, per input table: the declared ones and those inferred.

inferred.description: The bounds sverify inferred, per input table.

ensures.description: Each postcondition, in the order given, as a finding: kind pass where it is proved, fail where not.

issues.description: The runtime errors the checker could not rule out, as findings.

assumed.description: The SUMs assumed to fit their type and the double operations assumed to stay finite, each checked on the data while the job runs: findings of level note, kind informational, with properties.assumption.

needs.description: The preconditions the proof needs that requires does not state (Report.needs); empty unless on_inferred is "error".

facts.description: What the checker established about each output column (Report.facts): in words, whether it may be NULL, and inclusive bounds on its non-NULL values, written as counterexample values are. A report written before #704 has the words alone.

not_null.description: The output columns the checker proved never NULL (not nullable in Report.output), in the output's order.

output.description: The output's columns with their Ibis types.

routes.description: The route each engine ran the plan by, by engine name; empty until the report's plan runs.

ties.description: Where the plan leaves its result open at the exact level (class picks included, kind "class"), and the sv.unique(...) per input table that would determine the result. The keys are confirmed together, so they belong to all places.

kind.description: tie: the order of ties is open; class: a pick among the members of a class of doubles (D48); open: what the class level leaves open.

dialect_differences.description: For SQL, where the reference reads the text differently from DuckDB: the construct, where it is, both readings, an example and the spellings that mean the same under both semantics.

rewrites.description: The rewrites of the optimized plan.

run_gate.description: The gate that kept the plan as written in place of the rewrite (#1787), or null where the engine runs the rewrite.

implied.description: A SQL condition per input table that every row reaching the result passes.

transfer.description: Under semantics="substrait", the options where the reference's proof does not carry over; null under the other profiles.

engines.description: Per engine, the checker's verdict on the plan (substrait-check --contract's "engines"): its class, evidence and what refuses it. Null in a report from a checker without it.

checker.description: The checker that proved the plan. generated_proofs: whether its generated lift and lowering proofs were checked (substrait-check --build); false for a plain lake build, an editable install or a borrowed binary, which hold them as sorry. Null where the checker does not say, and in a report written before 1.0.

sorted.description: Whether the plan's result comes out of a sort, as the checker reads it.

depends.description: The options the proof depends on (substrait-check --contract's "depends").

black_boxes.description: The black boxes the transformation calls, in the order of first call, each with the laws its row declares: what the proofs trust of them (substrait-check --contract's "black_boxes", #1484). Report.black_boxes maps each name to its laws.

floats_on.description: Per engine, why its doubles may not meet the equivalence (empty where they do).

value.description: What the checker established about the condition, such as "TRUE or NULL".

checked.description: Checked on the output data instead (on_unproved="check").

needs.description: For an unproved condition, preconditions requires does not state under which it is proved (CheckedCondition.needs): those its proof used where sverify inferred them (reason needs), or those the checker suggests. A sufficient set, not claimed minimal.

counterexample.description: Inputs that meet the preconditions on which the condition fails. Values are JSON's own; NaN, infinities, decimals, dates, times and bytes (as hex) are text.

shown.description: The operation in the user's terms.

needs.description: The preconditions that rule it out; table is null where the inference does not name it.

value.description: The bound as a SQL literal.

code.description: The condition as the Python a user writes in requires.

needed.description: A precondition, as Report.needs lists them. A suggestion carries only table and label.

kind.description: The route taken; null for a refusal. 1.x may add values.

class.description: The plan's class on the engine. 1.x may add values.

facts.description: The engine facts behind the choices the class rests on.

theorems.description: The Lean theorems that prove those choices, where they are proved.

version.description: The engine version the facts were probed at.

issues.description: The issues that track the tested choices.

proved_facts.description: The facts the theorems rest on, where they prove the engine's model.

semantics.description: The semantics the proof the run relies on is under.

equivalence.description: What the result's consumer can tell apart (sv.equivalent): its text and its components; a tolerance on doubles is {abs, rel, ulps}.

finding.description: A SARIF 2.1.0 result (#793): a tool wraps these in a SARIF run for `sverify check --format sarif`. 1.x may add locations and fixes.

ruleId.description: The finding's code, snake_case: a postcondition's reason (or proved), an issue's kind (division_by_zero, sum_overflow). 1.x may add values.

level.description: SARIF's level: error where the proof fails, warning where the data is checked instead or the operation need not raise, note where it holds with a caveat or is assumed, none where it holds.

text.description: The finding in words, as str(report) prints it.

locations.description: Where the finding is in the source, as SARIF locations. Not written yet.

fixes.description: Verified fixes, as SARIF fixes. Not written yet.
